title: Pure Elements
welcome_lead: Meet the building blocks: substances made of only one type of atom.
meta_desc: Discover what elements are and how they appear on the periodic table in this KS3 chemistry adventure.
final_note: You now know that elements are the purest form of matter.

concepts.def: A substance made of only one type of atom.
The tiny building block of all matter.
One or two letters that represent an element, like O or Fe.
Made of only one type of particle throughout.
A chart of all known elements.
Existing as pairs of atoms bonded together, like O2.

walkthroughs.body_html:
An element is a substance made of only one type of atom. You cannot break an element down into anything simpler using chemistry.

One element = one type of atom.

Every element has a chemical symbol. Examples: H (hydrogen), O (oxygen), Fe (iron), Na (sodium), Au (gold).

The first letter is always a capital, the second is always lowercase.

Copper wires, gold jewellery, helium balloons, the oxygen in your lungs and the carbon in pencil lead are all elements.

There are about 118 known elements organised on the periodic table.
